title: Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat Records Cumulative Sales Cross Rs 73.49 Lakh, Reflecting Growing Public Appreciation for Artisans' Products
subtitle:
Mela Draws Enthusiastic Public Participation, Celebrates India's Cultural Diversity
More Than 130 Stalls Showcase Traditional Handicrafts, Handloom Products and Indigenous Creations Across Seven Thematic Zones
Daily Cultural Performances, Traditional Music and Folk Dances Create a Vibrant Festive Atmosphere
body_text: The ongoing Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA, in the National Capital, is witnessing enthusiastic participation from citizens, families and young visitors, offering a vibrant celebration of India's traditional craftsmanship, cultural heritage and artistic diversity. The growing public interest is also reflected in the sales recorded during the Mela. A Senior Official in Ministry said the four participating National Corporations under the Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, have recorded cumulative sales of approximately ₹ 73.49  Lakh between November 1 and November 10, 2026. The sales reflect the encouraging response from visitors and the increasing market opportunities for products created by beneficiary communities. The four participating corporations include National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) and National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC), he said. Organised by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, the 15-day Mela has emerged as an engaging platform where visitors explore indigenous products, experience regional art forms and connect with the country's rich cultural traditions. Organised around the theme ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’, the Mela brings together traditional craftsmanship and cultural heritage through seven thematic zones: कला आँगन, प्रकाश चौक, पूजा पथ, सजावट बाज़ार, घराना, स्वाद चौक and मंच. Each zone offers visitors a distinctive experience, covering traditional crafts, festive decorations, home décor, cultural products and regional culinary traditions. The Official said the Mela features more than 130 stalls showcasing a diverse range of handicrafts, handloom products, traditional textiles, lamps, festive decorations, home décor items and other indigenous creations. The visitors are enthusiastically exploring the stalls, appreciating the craftsmanship of participating artisans and purchasing products that reflect India's rich artistic traditions, he added. A major attraction of the Mela is its lively cultural programme organised every evening at the Manch. Artists and performing troupes from different States are presenting colourful folk dances, traditional music and regional art forms, bringing together diverse cultural expressions on a common platform. These performances offer visitors an opportunity to experience India's cultural richness and regional traditions while creating a festive atmosphere of celebration and cultural exchange. The cultural evenings have added a distinctive dimension to the Mela, making it more than an exhibition and shopping destination. Visitors are enjoying the performances, discovering different regional traditions and experiencing the artistic diversity that reflects India's pluralistic cultural identity. The Mela provides a valuable marketing platform for artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase their products and connect directly with consumers. The Ministry facilitates their participation by providing free stalls, travel expenses, daily allowances and transportation facilities for their goods, helping them overcome logistical and financial barriers. The initiative also promotes wider market access through platforms such as Bharat TULIP, which connects artisans with e-commerce opportunities, and Purple Fest, which celebrates the creativity and capabilities of persons with disabilities while encouraging inclusion and equal opportunities. Since 2022, the Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas, benefiting more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamchari communities by providing opportunities to exhibit and market their products. The initiative aims to encourage self-employment, strengthen entrepreneurship and promote socio-economic empowerment through sustainable livelihood opportunities. The Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 will continue at Dilli Haat, INA, New Delhi, until November 15, 2026. Through its combination of traditional products, cultural performances and public participation, the Mela offers a meaningful platform for celebrating India's artistic diversity while advancing the vision of an inclusive and self-reliant India. *** PR-219-TAR/KV/GA/RK
